setup.article: Article 12 - establishing and maintaining a due diligence system, reporting annually on due diligence system, keeping records on due diligence
setup.label:
Develop detailed EUDR due diligence compliance framework including policies, procedures, standard operating procedures for:
 -data collection/storage (HS codes, geolocation, volumes)
- data collection methods and verification
 -maintaining and updating supply chain information and documentation
- risk assessment protocols based on regulatory points
- risk mitigation strategies including identifying and mitigating non-negligible risks (additional documentation, supplier audits)
- DDS preparation and integration with batch-tracking
-DDS submission systems
- supplier engagement

Establish information/data systems for EUDR compliance including:
- IT systems for data collection/storage (HS codes, geolocation, volumes)
 - IT infrastructure for product/batch data tagging (geolocations, dates)
- Establishment of  automated/manual DDS submission systems

Conduct staff training and ensure sufficient capacity to manage EUDR compliance, including
-  due diligence system operations
- data collection methods and verification
- evaluating reliability and credibility of evidence
- identifying and mitigating non-negligible risks
- DDS preparation and integration with batch-tracking

setup.article: Article 9: Information collection: product, product origin (e.g. geolocation), supplier and customer, evidence to support legal and deforestation-free status of relevant commodity at point of production
setup.label:
Investigate and confirm product scope (HS Codes/ingredients)
- is the company placing on the market or making availale for sale relevant comodities that fall under Annex 1?
Collect / maintain Article 9 information excluding the separately identified geolocation effort; include customer name, address and email and passing on DDS references.

setup.article: Article 9 - Geolocation data gathering, plot verification & GIS tooling
setup.label: Supplier engagement for plot data, file checking, corrections, tooling

setup.article: Article 10 - Risk Assessment: Verification of  evidence to support legal and deforestation-free status of relevant commodity at point of production to 'negligable risk'
setup.label:
Conduct initial risk assessments 
- prioritise high-risk countries/supply chains
- risk assessment against EUDR criteria , to provide  "adequately conclusive and verifiable information that the relevant products are deforestation-free have been produced in accordance with the relevant legislation of the country of production"
- risk remaining must be 'no or negligable'
- develop risk mitigation interventions

setup.article: Article 11 Risk mitigation: Required only for material originating from standard and high risk countries, where risk has been assessed and identified as more than negligible. Where the risk is identified as non-negligible, products cannot be placed on the market until risk can be assessed as zero or negligible.
setup.label:
Risk mitigation
- Implement initial mitigation actions for identified risks, could include:
 - additional information collection,on the ground auditing, product testing, supplier exclusion and seeking alternatives

setup.article: Article 3 and annex 1, submitting due diligence statements.
setup.label: Submit initial DDS for existing products/batches

setup.label: Establish business, product, estimated quantity and country-of-production records
setup.notes: Reference business: small UK primary producer (low risk, 2025/1093), owner-managed with a farm office, 5 to 10 plots, placing or exporting its own produce. Owner time at PM rate, office time at AA rate. Confirm Annex I scope and HS codes (PM 0.5); confirm Article 2(15a) status (PM 0.25); EORI number for cross-border movements (AA 0.25); compile Annex III business, product, quantity and country-of-production record (AA 0.5). Size factor: days are for a small business undiscounted; see note to Daniel on Section 4 size for this block.

setup.label: Record plot postal address or geolocation; Adam to specify the chosen approach
setup.notes: Annex III: geolocation or postal address of every plot or establishment; Article 4a(5) allows the address. Compile the plot list from holding and field records (AA 0.5, PM 0.5). Woodland parcels and detached land often have no postal address: PM 0.5 to extract coordinates or a polygon from Rural Payments field-parcel data or the Land Registry title plan. Address-based reference with coordinates where no address exists. AE3 does not touch this row.

setup.label: Submit one-time simplified declaration, directly or through first customer
setup.notes: Register for EU Login and the information system (AA 0.5); complete and submit the declaration and record the identifier (PM 0.5, AA 0.25); pass the identifier to customers (AA 0.25). Article 4a(2) also allows submission through the first customer, costed in the downstream blocks. EC set at 0 (producer self-registers); revisit after interviews, alternative EC 0.5 for a land agent or trade-association adviser.

ongoing.label: Maintain business and production records; no rolling DDS
ongoing.notes: Keep the Annex III record and declaration identifier on file; answer customer requests for the identifier; check annually that products, quantity band and plots are as declared (PM 0.25, AA 0.5). Assisting a competent-authority check is included: Article 16(9) low-risk check rate is 1% of operators a year, so expected effort is a fraction of a day. No rolling DDS.

ongoing.label: Update plot address / production information where needed; Adam to define effort
ongoing.notes: Article 4a(3): update after a major change only (new plots, new products, change of quantity band). Expected annual effort 1 day (PM 0.5, AA 0.5), allowing for roughly one update every two to three years plus re-issuing the identifier to customers.

setup.label: Establish supplier-details capture
setup.notes:
Reference business: large downstream operator or trader, over 250 staff, about 50 operator suppliers, 400 receipts a year, several commodities, ERP master data, compliance function and legal access. Size factor 1. Article 5(3)(a) supplier name, postal address and email: one tenth of operator row 11 by role (SO 2, PM 2, AA 1, IT 0.5, EC 0.5): add fields to supplier master data, write to suppliers, chase and load responses. The operator's product, origin and evidence effort falls away.
8 November implementation: Reference role-days preserved. Working_table scales this task by modelled/reference supplier count (Working B105). Other tasks are fixed unless separately specified.

setup.label: Establish capture of DDS references or declaration identifiers
setup.notes: Own days, no operator equivalent. DDS reference numbers or declaration identifiers, required only where the supplier is an operator. Define the process with suppliers and purchasing terms (SO 2, PM 2), add the field to goods-receipt or purchase-order records (IT 2), test and brief staff (AA 1).

setup.label: Establish customer-details capture
setup.notes: Article 5(3)(b): name, postal address and email of each downstream operator or trader supplied. Sales master data holds most of this already (SO 1, AA 1, IT 0.5).

setup.label: Establish five-year record retention
setup.notes: Article 5(4): keep the Article 5(3) information at least five years and provide on request. One tenth of operator row 8 (SO 2, AA 0.5, IT 3): retention rule, archive location, retrieval procedure.

setup.label: Register once in the EU information system
setup.notes: Own days. One-time registration in the information system before placing or exporting: EU Login, registration, record of the identifier (SO 1, AA 0.5).

setup.label: Establish contingent concern checks and authority-notification procedures
setup.notes: Own days. Procedure for informing competent authorities and customers on a concrete indication (5(5)) and, on a substantiated concern, verifying that due diligence was exercised and the risk is negligible before proceeding (5(6)). Draft, legal review, sign-off (SO 2, LAW 1, PM 1).

ongoing.label: Capture supplier details
ongoing.notes:
New and changed suppliers at 10% churn a year: one tenth of operator row 21 (SO 1.5, PM 1, AA 1).
8 November implementation: Reference role-days preserved. Working_table scales this task by modelled/reference supplier count (Working B105). Other tasks are fixed unless separately specified.

ongoing.label: Capture DDS references or declaration identifiers
ongoing.notes:
Volume-driven. 400 receipts a year at ten minutes each to record the reference number, about 8 AA days, plus SO 2 to chase missing or mismatched references. Assumes the reference arrives on the supplier's commercial documents. First item to test in interviews.
8 November implementation: Reference role-days preserved. Working_table scales this task by modelled/reference annual receipts (Working B108). Other tasks are fixed unless separately specified.

ongoing.notes: Keep records and the Article 5(2) registration current; assist checks under Article 5(7) and Article 19 (3% check rate for standard-risk countries, Article 16(8)). About 15% of operator row 19 (SO 1, AA 0.5, IT 1).

ongoing.label: Contingent check and inform activity; annual expected effort
ongoing.notes: Expected annual effort: one substantiated concern every two years at five days (SO 3, LAW 1, PM 1), giving SO 1.5, LAW 0.5, PM 0.5. Frequency is an assumption for the interviews to test.

behavior_notes: Role-days are person-days. Calculate with full unrounded salary day rates; round only presentation.
Low-risk operators retain annual training and Article 9 information/geolocation; only Article 10/11 task rows13,14,23,24 are excluded.
Information tasks exclude the geolocation allocation. Changing the allocation subtracts it from the fixed Article9 role budget, then geolocation is added only when enabled.
AE4 divides only variable DDS role-days. Fixed role-days are never batched.
Local-laws factor is 1 - legality_share*(1-land_use_retained). It scales annual Art10/11 and initial Art10/11 only when setup switch is on.
Primary eligibility is micro/small and low risk only. Apply primary_complexity and optional micro factor only, bypassing operator DD/commodity and generic size factors.
Downstream ignores DD, commodity and supply-chain-depth factors. Apply supplier ratios only to rows51,59,69,76 and receipt ratios only to rows60,77; other task costs stay fixed.
Downstream SME size factors remain medium.9, small.75, micro.5. Reference inputs built at30suppliers/200receipts are preserved.
Defra applies year3 reduction once to all applicable groups. Among three comparison scenarios, only comparison2 shows year3 output. Total means setup plus one annual cost.
User-adjustable tasks without assigned time require explicit zero; blank inputs must not silently understate totals.
Cost task-day totals for downstream remain raw input days even when Working cost totals use changed volume ratios.
